Fetch your pull requests, commits, and reviews from GitHub. Standup reports then count the activity that no done entry links to.

## CLI: gournal sync

Fetch your GitHub activity (PRs, commits, reviews) through the gh CLI. Gournal links the activity to your entries.

```text
gournal sync [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--since <date>` | Fetch activity from this date. Use a local day or an ISO timestamp. Without this option, gournal starts at the stored sync cursor. With no cursor, it starts github.initialSyncDays days before now. |

## MCP tool: sync_activity

Fetch the user's GitHub activity (PRs, commits, reviews) through the gh CLI, and link it to journal entries. The gh CLI must be signed in.

### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `since` | `string` | no | Fetch activity from this date: a local day (YYYY-MM-DD) or an ISO timestamp. Without this option, gournal fetches from the last sync. |

### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `status` | `"ok" \| "partial" \| "skipped" \| "failed"` | yes | ok: the sync finished. partial: the sync stopped early and kept what it fetched. skipped: an automatic sync did not run because another sync held the lock. Only automatic sync returns skipped. The sync_activity tool returns ok, partial, or failed. failed: the sync did not run, for example when gh is missing or signed out. |
| `since` | `string` | yes | Start of the fetched window, as an ISO timestamp. |
| `inserted` | `number` | yes | Number of new activity items stored. |
| `updated` | `number` | yes | Number of known activity items that changed. |
| `linked` | `number` | yes | Number of links that gournal made between activity items and entries. |
| `warning` | `string \| null` | yes | Why the sync stopped or failed, or null. |

## Examples

### CLI

Fetch GitHub activity through the gh CLI. This example uses a stand-in gh program with fixture data for the `acme` and `octo` owners.

```console
$ gournal sync --since 2026-11-01
Synced GitHub activity since Nov 01: 4 new, 0 updated, 3 links.
```

After an earlier sync worked, a later sync without a working gh CLI reports why it stopped. A new user who never synced sees `GitHub sync failed (gh is not installed; see https://cli.github.com)` instead.

```console
$ gournal sync
Synced GitHub activity since Nov 15: 0 new, 0 updated, 0 links. Stopped early (gh is not installed; see https://cli.github.com); run gournal sync again to continue.
```
